data.content_ref: inline:The proposed 'shared mechanism' is causally underspecified because the relation hinges on 'enumerate-and-test near the mean' as a common machinery, yet the target provides no causal account of why the inverted direction (refutation via failed search vs. confirmation via successful search) preserves the same mechanism rather than producing two structurally distinct procedures. The problem demands a substantive relation with a stated mechanism; calling both 'enumerate-and-test' collapses the causal distinction the target itself foregrounds — confirmation terminates on a satisfiable witness whereas refutation-by-uniqueness requires exhaustive failure, a different stopping condition that changes the procedure's logical role. Without explaining how the shared search step survives this directional inversion, the relation reduces to a label overlap ('enumerate candidates, test parity') rather than a demonstrated shared causal mechanism.
